control_device_fabrication: The PSCs achieved a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 16.996% under an active area of 0.09 cm², with a VOC value of 0.98403 V, an FF value of 87.172%, and a current density (JSC) of 19.814 mA/cm². A solution of Cs0.1FA0.9I2.8Br0.2 at 1.5 mol/L provided the foundational matrix for the perovskite layer. The optimal SAM was prepared by using Me-4PACz (0.33 mg/mL).The sample of Me-4PACz was fabricated with a concentration of 0.33 mg/mL. The perovskite precursor solution was prepared by mixing 2.5 mg/mL of MACl additive in the solvent. To ensure uniform film deposition, we utilized a double spin stage, starting at 1200 rpm (10 s) and subsequently 5000 rpm (30 s). Antisolvent (200 µL) was dripped onto the center of film at 8 s before the end of spin-coating. Heat-treatment was implemented with the substrates for 30 min at 110 °C.
target_device_fabrication: By refining specific fabrication parameters, a perovskite solar cell was meticulously prepared, culminating in performance metrics including a PCE of 17.726%, FF of 87.146%, Voc of 0.96559 V, and Jsc of 21.065 mA/cm². The perovskite precursor solution with a molar concentration of 1.5 mol/L was prepared according to the formula of Cs0.1FA0.9I2.8Br0.2. Controlled addition of Me-4PACz (0.33 mg/mL) as a SAM was performed to stabilize the perovskite layer and engineer a more robust interface. The incorporation of MACl (10.0 mg/mL) additive was ensured. The perovskite film was deposited by spin-coating onto the substrate using two-step spin-coating process, first at 1200 rpm for 10 s and then at 5000 rpm for 30 s. The addition of 200 µL antisolvent at last 8 s proved instrumental in achieving uniform film thickness and grain distribution. The perovskite film was annealed at 110 °C for 30 min.
